prose.def: To carry or lead someone or something up, or to bring an offering up to an altar.
prose.article: ἀναφέρω literally means to carry something up, used in the Gospels when Jesus leads disciples up a mountain (Matthew 17:1, Mark 9:2) or is taken up into heaven (Luke 24:51). It also developed a sacrificial sense, bringing offerings up to an altar, which dominates the Septuagint, where it appears 149 times and often renders the Hebrew word for a burnt offering (עֹלָה, 63×). One intriguing detail: Deissmann argued from everyday papyri that 1 Peter 2:24 may echo a legal usage about transferring one person's debts onto another.

prose.def: To cry out loudly or exclaim, raising one's voice in a strong, emphatic utterance.
prose.article: ἀναφωνέω means to raise the voice and cry out, built from ἀνά (up) and φωνέω (to make a sound). It appears just once in the New Testament, at Luke 1:42, where Elizabeth "exclaimed" with a loud voice — the only New Testament occurrence, rendered the same way by both the Majority Standard Bible and the Berean Standard Bible. Interestingly, in the Septuagint it most often translates the Hebrew word for cymbals (4 of 5 times), pointing to a loud, sounding-out quality, while the everyday papyri show a weakened sense, as in a Fayum document of 124 B.C. where it refers to a crown tax being formally "decreed."
prose.caution: This word occurs only once in the New Testament, and the sources note differing senses (the lexica also cite Hebrew counterparts that disagree with the digest's listed ones), so confidence in its full range is low.
